bull_bear.body: Debt reduction prioritized (net debt down to INR 3,646cr); capex focused on value-added capacity and decarbonization; no dividend or buyback mentioned; consolidation of subsidiaries (Chromeni, RVPL, RT) planned over next 1-2 years
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: QCO suspension until Dec 2025 enabling cheap imports; CBAM uncertainty delaying export recovery; global demand softness in US/EU; ferrochrome price volatility; land acquisition delays for Maharashtra plant; potential margin pressure from import competition
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; focused on execution, quality, and sustainability; cautious on guidance revisions due to external uncertainties; proactive on policy advocacy (QCO, PLI); optimistic on long-term infrastructure demand and green transition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 6,700 fabricators trained in Q2 (cumulative 60,400) — building ecosystem lock-in for stainless steel in infra; green hydrogen plant (600 NMQ/hr) is among India’s largest planned for steel; Sukinda mine (own chrome ore) to start FY27 — rare backward integration in Indian stainless steel
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt has been reduced across the disclosed dates: INR 3,991 cr (Mar'25), INR 3,040 cr (Mar'26) and INR 2,950 cr (Jun'26); net debt here includes only bank and financial institution loans.
- Total debt of INR 6,649 cr at June 2026 (long term INR 4,642 cr, short term INR 2,006 cr) against cash & bank balances of INR 3,698 cr; short-term debt has risen from INR 1,107 cr at Mar'25 to INR 2,006 cr at Jun'26 while long-term debt has fallen from INR 5,169 cr.
- Leverage is low and improving: Net Debt/Equity of 0.14x and Net Debt/EBITDA of 0.53x at Jun'26, versus 0.15x and 0.55x at Mar'26 and 0.24x and 0.86x at Mar'25.
- Net worth (including non-controlling interest) has grown from INR 16,708 cr (Mar'25) to INR 19,882 cr (Mar'26) to INR 20,672 cr (Jun'26), with ROE reported at 16% (Mar'25) and 17% (Mar'26 and Jun'26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Flat products: 34% 200-series, 49% 300-series, 17% 400-series; long products: rebar sales rising (2,000-2,500 tons/month), wire rod moderating; fabrication: new Patalganga unit operational; exports: subdued due to CBAM uncertainty; NPI: EBITDA positive, $500-1,500/ton range; Chromeni: 70% utilization, targeting 80% in H2

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as India's leading stainless steel manufacturer with an annual turnover of INR 42,955 crore (USD 4.86 billion) in FY26 and an annual melt capacity of 4.2 million tonnes.
- Global footprint as of March 2026: 16 stainless steel manufacturing and processing facilities in India and abroad, including in Spain and Indonesia, and a worldwide network in 12 countries.
- Domestic distribution reach of ten sales offices and six service centres in India as of March 2026; founded in 1970.
- Balance-sheet standing reinforced by long term debt ratings of AA/Positive and short term debt ratings of A1+.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Shareholding] As of 30th June 2026: Promoters 62.0%, FII 20.5%, Retail & others 10.1% and DII 7.4% (the deck labels the non-promoter block as Other 38.0%).
- [Associates] The consolidated P&L includes a share of profit from associates of Rs 35 crore in Q1 FY27 versus a loss of Rs 14 crore in Q1 FY26, indicating a material associate-level business outside the consolidated operating entity.
- [Scope] The disclaimer describes the document as a "joint earning presentation" prepared for "respective company(ies)", while the financials presented are consolidated Jindal Stainless Limited.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved YoY despite soft exports; nickel prices stable; cost advantage from 42% renewable energy use (up from 26% in FY25); QCO suspension pressures pricing; ferrochrome cost benefit expected from Sukinda mine (starting FY27)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 9-10% YoY maintained; margin: unchanged; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: FY26 capex guidance INR 2,700cr (H1 spent INR 1,260cr); NPI at 90%, Chromeni ramping to 80% in H2, SMS Indonesia early FY27, cold rolling end FY27, HRAP H2 FY27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Fabrication unit (Jindal Stainless Steelway) unlocks infrastructure EPC opportunities; green hydrogen plant (600 NMQ/hr) at Jajpur to cut emissions; PLI scheme potential in stainless flats/longs; stainless rebar adoption in bridges and public infra; export potential if CBAM clarity emerges
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Strong domestic demand and value-added product growth drove 15% YoY volume growth and 33% PAT growth, while green hydrogen and fabrication unit launches signal strategic shift toward high-margin, sustainable infrastructure solutions; however, CBAM uncertainty and QCO suspension remain key external headwinds.

open.item: Commission a 0.17 MTPA Cold Rolled Annealed Pickled (CRAP) line at Jajpur, Odisha by Q2 FY27, as part of the previously announced INR 1,900 crore investment.
Commission a 1.1 MTPA Hot Rolled Annealed Pickled (HRAP) line at Jajpur, Odisha by Q4 FY27, as part of the previously announced INR 1,900 crore investment.
Fund an INR 2,600 crore capex programme in FY27 from the existing balance sheet.
Invest INR 900 crore to strengthen cold rolling capabilities at Hisar and Kharagpur, with commissioning planned by Q2 FY28.
Raise CRAP capacity from 2.05 MTPA in FY26 to 2.67 MTPA by FY28, enabling thinner cold-rolled products for high-growth sectors.

Lift cold rolling capacity from 2.05 MTPA to 2.67 MTPA by FY28 through the INR 900 crore investment across Hisar and Kharagpur plus new hot rolled annealing, pickling and cold rolling facilities at Jajpur.
Increase CRAP capacity from 2.05 MTPA to 2.67 MTPA by FY28 to support a richer value-added product mix.
Achieve sales volumes of 3.5 MTPA by FY29.
Progress plans for a new integrated stainless steel project in Maharashtra alongside strengthening downstream capacity.
Strengthen long-term raw material security through backward integration — chrome ore linkage with Odisha Mining Corporation (OMC) and development of captive mining assets at Sukinda.

Jindal Stainless Steelway Limited (JSSL) is investing in a dedicated stainless steel fabrication plant to strengthen end-to-end capability, after the infrastructure segment grew from a single project in 2021 to 20+ executed stainless steel infrastructure projects nationally.
Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) plant imported in 2025-26 to reduce fresh water consumption through water recycling is under commissioning.
Green Hydrogen plant imported in 2025-26 to enable cleaner, more efficient annealing is under commissioning (Directors' Report technology-absorption disclosure).

Develop a 315.6 MW solar-wind hybrid renewable energy project in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat with Oyster Renewable Energy at an investment of INR 132 crore by the Company, expected to abate around 6.5 lakh metric tonnes of carbon emissions per year once fully operational.
Double slag processing capacity at Jajpur through a new wet milling plant with Harsco Environmental, involving an investment of USD 150 million under a 15-year agreement.

Explore an investment of INR 40,000 crore to set up a stainless steel manufacturing facility in Maharashtra under a non-binding MoU signed in FY25 with the state government, with the project to be developed over the next decade.
INR 700+ crore committed to decarbonisation projects across operations.

risks.note: Dependence on nickel, ferrochrome and scrap prices exposes the Company to global commodity price volatility and supply fluctuations, which can impact raw material costs and margins. Mitigated through diversified domestic and international sourcing, long-term supplier partnerships, a joint venture securing nickel pig iron, and a ferrochrome mix of scrap, captive mines and supplies from Odisha Mining Corporation.
risks.risk: Raw material price risk — nickel, ferrochrome and scrap

risks.note: Low-cost imports, especially from China and FTA-linked markets, create pricing pressure and affect domestic competitiveness. The response is new grades, expanded applications, support for BIS standards and Quality Control Orders, and portfolio diversification.
risks.risk: Import risk — low-cost imports and pricing pressure

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, natural disasters and global disruptions may impact logistics and raw material availability; mitigated by a diversified supplier base, more domestic and regional sourcing, and flexible procurement.

Changes in environmental, product-quality and industry regulations may impact compliance requirements and operating costs. The Company monitors regulatory change, prepares for early compliance and participates in policy discussion including the proposed National Stainless Steel Policy.
Exposure to interest rate fluctuations and foreign exchange volatility arising from import-export operations; managed through disciplined leverage, refinancing and maturity management, and hedging.
risks.risk: Financial risk — interest rates and foreign exchange

risks.note: Increasing digitalisation raises exposure to cyber threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; addressed via cybersecurity systems, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, regular security audits, employee training and structured incident response.

Regulatory shifts such as CBAM and dependence on imported critical inputs like nickel increase climate-related risk. Mitigation runs through renewable energy, low-emission technologies, higher scrap usage, circular-economy practice, backward integration, stronger carbon accounting and evaluation of green hydrogen and electrification.

With employees and contract workers across multiple plant locations, any significant safety incident or regulatory non-compliance can cause operational disruption, production losses, higher absenteeism and attrition, and reputational damage. Managed under a 'No Harm' / 'Zero Harm' philosophy with LTIFR and fatality monitoring, safety training, and Spirometry/Audiometry health surveillance in dust-prone and high-noise environments.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across a large, geographically dispersed workforce (BRSR material issue 8)

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.
